Iran-US tensions rise after leader's death, new threats exchanged

Following the death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, tensions between Iran and the United States have escalated. His son, Mojtaba Khamenei, has vowed to avenge his father's death, stating it is the Iranian nation's demand and will be fulfilled. US President Donald Trump has issued a warning, stating he would obliterate Iran if it attacked him. Large crowds gathered in Iran for Khamenei's funeral, with some participants chanting anti-Trump slogans. Iran has also warned of strong retaliation against any counter-actions and has declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, threatening ships passing through.
